```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE,
  purl = FALSE
)
```

OneClickCartographics turns a plain occurrence table (species, latitude,
longitude) into a publication-ready distribution map with a single function
call. The map scale adapts automatically to the extent of your points, from
micro-local to global.

## The minimalistic default map

A CSV or Excel file with at least three columns -- species (or any grouping
column), latitude and longitude -- is all you need:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
library(OneClickCartographics)
run_map("my_localities.csv")
```

Alternatively, you can query GBIF directly by providing a scientific name:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("Panthera onca", journal = "zootaxa")
```

Every run writes an HTML report (`00_map_report.html`) formatted in the signature Orangutan-R HTML style next to the maps, recording map thumbnails, input data, records, projection, scale tier, base layers, and reproducible Materials & Methods prose with BibTeX citations.

## Automatic scale selection

The extent of the points decides the cartographic style:

* **Local** (span <= 300 km): Natural Earth 1:10m layers, UTM projection,
  populated places and roads on.
* **Regional** (300-3,000 km): 1:50m layers, UTM projection.
* **Continental** (3,000-8,000 km): 1:50m layers, Lambert Azimuthal
  Equal-Area projection centered on the data.
* **Global** (> 8,000 km or dateline-crossing): 1:110m layers, World
  Equidistant Cylindrical (EPSG:4087); the antimeridian is handled
  automatically for Pacific species.

You can always override the automatic choice:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", scale = 10, projection = 32614)
```

## Multiple species

With two or more groups in the colour column, each group is drawn with a
distinct colour **and** shape combination, with a single combined legend.
Scientific names are automatically italicized in the legend:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("several_species.csv")
```

Use `color_by` to group by any other column (population, year, museum...) and
`shape_by` to map an additional column to point shapes.

## Colour palettes

The default palette is Okabe-Ito (colour-blind safe). You can use viridis,
RColorBrewer, or a custom set of colours:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# viridis palettes
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = "viridis")
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = "magma")

# RColorBrewer palettes
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = "Set1")
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = "Paired")

# custom hex colours
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = c("#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#0000FF"))

# from a file (one hex colour per line)
run_map("my_localities.csv", palette = "my_colours.txt")
```

## Legend position

Control where the legend appears on the map:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", legend_position = "right")
run_map("my_localities.csv", legend_position = "left")
run_map("my_localities.csv", legend_position = "none")  # hide legend
```

## GIS export

Export occurrence points (and optional density grid) as GIS vector files:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# shapefile
run_map("my_localities.csv", gis_formats = "shp")

# GeoPackage and GeoJSON
run_map("my_localities.csv", gis_formats = c("gpkg", "geojson"))

# with density grid
run_map("my_localities.csv", grid_km = 25, gis_formats = "gpkg")
```

Output files are saved to the output directory as `{filename}_points.{ext}`
and `{filename}_grid.{ext}`.

## Grid analysis

The density grid can be limited to a custom bounding box and exported as a CSV
with per-species counts:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Full-extent grid with 25 km cells
run_map("my_localities.csv", grid_km = 25)

# Grid limited to a specific region
run_map("my_localities.csv", grid_km = 25,
        grid_bbox = c(-100, -80, 30, 45))

# Export grid counts (per-species and total) to CSV
run_map("my_localities.csv", grid_km = 25, grid_csv = TRUE)
```

The output `grid_counts.csv` contains columns: `grid_id`, `lon_center`,
`lat_center` (cell centre coordinates in the projected CRS), `total`, and one
column per species with the count of records in that cell.

## Graticule control

The graticule can be toggled off entirely or shown as full lines instead of
tick-only labels:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# No graticule at all
run_map("my_localities.csv", graticule = FALSE)

# Full graticule lines (above points)
run_map("my_localities.csv", graticule_lines = TRUE)
```

When `graticule = TRUE` (default), only axis tick labels are shown. Set
`graticule_lines = TRUE` to draw full coordinate lines across the map. Lines
are drawn as the topmost layer, above points and grids.

## Optional layers to understand biodiversity

All optional layers are off by default and skip gracefully when unavailable
(no internet, missing suggested packages).

Altitude map (SRTM elevation with a terrain colour scale):

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", show_elevation = TRUE)
```

Land + ocean topography (ETOPO1 global relief, elevation and bathymetry in
one two-sided scale; downloaded once and cached):

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", show_topo = TRUE)
```

WWF terrestrial ecoregions (thin outlines under the points; downloaded once
and cached):

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", show_ecoregions = TRUE)
```

Density grid (records per square cell; the points themselves are never
modified, `show_points = FALSE` hides them):

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("dense_download.csv", grid_km = 25)
```

## Advanced biodiversity features

### Direct GBIF querying

You can query occurrence records directly from GBIF by providing a scientific binomial:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("Panthera onca", journal = "zootaxa", preset = "2col")
```

### Automated coordinate quality cleaning

Flag and drop problematic coordinates (Null Island, inverted lat/lon, placeholder grids):

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", clean_coords = TRUE)
```

### IUCN Red List Range Assessment (Criterion B)

Calculate Extent of Occurrence (EOO) and Area of Occupancy (AOO) with automated habitat constraints:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv",
        iucn = TRUE,
        show_eoo = TRUE,
        iucn_medium = "land")
```

### Highlighting taxonomic type specimens

Emphasize Holotypes and Syntypes with prominent gold diamond markers:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("taxonomic_sample.csv", highlight_type = TRUE)
```

### Journal dimension presets

Format maps to exact publisher guidelines:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("my_localities.csv", journal = "zootaxa", preset = "2col")
run_map("my_localities.csv", journal = "pensoft", preset = "1col")
run_map("my_localities.csv", journal = "nature", preset = "1.5col")
```

### Multi-species comparative plates

Facet multi-species occurrences into a single standardized plate:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
run_map("multi_species.csv", facet = TRUE, facet_by = "species", facet_cols = 2)
```

### Interactive web cartography

Inspect distribution data with interactive hover tooltips and popups:

```{r, eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
interactive_map("my_localities.csv", color_by = "species")
```

## Cartographic details

* Scale bar, north arrow and graticule are added by default.
* An optional inset locator map (`inset_map = TRUE`, requires `patchwork`).
* PDF, PNG and SVG output at your choice of resolution.
* Base layers: Natural Earth (public domain).

## Data requirements

* Input: `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, `.xlsx` or `.xls`.
* Columns: a species/grouping column, latitude and longitude. Latitude is
  taken from `lat`, `latitude` or `decimalLatitude`; longitude from `lon`,
  `long`, `longitude` or `decimalLongitude`.
* Optional columns: `typeStatus` / `type_status` for taxonomic highlighting.
* Rows with missing or out-of-range coordinates are dropped with a warning.
* The points are plotted as given unless `clean_coords = TRUE` is explicitly enabled.
